description: Trigger discrimination: goal-to-skill-set selection (this skill) vs beginner lifecycle routing (project-orchestrator), one-skill design quality (skill-quality-reviewer), catalog browsing/lookup (a documentation route), change classification (change-classification-gate), and a request that already names its skill.

cases.prompt: Given our goal of making this multi-tenant app launch-ready, which shipped Aegis skills should we use and in what order?
cases.reason: A stated outcome becomes a ranked set of existing skills with roles and order — no lifecycle stage detection and no single-skill quality verdict is requested.

cases.prompt: List the shipped meta skills and where each is documented.
cases.reason: Browse/lookup is answered by the catalog document, not a goal-to-shortlist. The selector's job is goal→shortlist; a catalogue lookup is a documentation route. EVAL-004 enforces that trigger-eval machine fields name only real skills/agents, so the route is encoded in expected_route (docs/skills-catalog.md) and NOT as a fabricated expected_skill — the plan's recorded structural-limitation contingency.
cases.note: ROUTE-TOKEN CASE — catalogue navigation is a documentation route, not an installed skill. To satisfy the live contract-audit EVAL-004 rule (trigger-eval machine fields must resolve to real skills/agents), expected_skill and overlaps_with deliberately name only real skills; expected_route carries the document route.

cases.prompt: I'm not a developer, I have an app idea but no project yet, and I don't know where to start.
cases.reason: With no defined stage, the request is lifecycle routing and requirements discovery from stage zero — the orchestrator's front-door job — not a shortlist of skills for a stated goal.

cases.prompt: Review whether this drafted skill's description is trigger-oriented and whether it collides with shipped skills.
cases.reason: One skill's design quality is the quality reviewer's judgment layer; the selector compares shipped skills for a goal, it does not judge a definition.

cases.prompt: Before I start this change, tell me which class it is and what validation floor applies — docs-only or AI/agentic behavior?
cases.reason: Classifying the change and setting its validation floor precedes any selection; the gate owns the class decision, the selector does not.

cases.prompt: Use the rls-policy-auditor skill to audit our database policies.
cases.reason: The user already names the skill and the task is one scoped step; a selector that re-routes a direct request adds friction and can silently substitute a different skill.
